name: Morgan House
summary: A 1930s stone mansion on Durpin hill, built for the jute baron George Morgan and now run by West Bengal Tourism (WBTDC). Lawns, ivy, fireplaces and a Kanchenjunga view, about 3 km above the town centre, at government-lodge rates.
body: Morgan House is the reason many people choose Kalimpong over Darjeeling. The house was built in the 1930s for George Morgan, an English jute baron, and passed to the state after Independence. West Bengal Tourism (WBTDC) runs it as a lodge, so you get a colonial country house with wooden floors, fireplaces and a long lawn for a fraction of what a private heritage hotel would charge. It sits on Durpin hill at about 1,370 m, close to the army golf course and the Zang Dhok Palri monastery, roughly 3 km from the Motor Stand.

Rooms vary a great deal, from small doubles to large deluxe rooms and cottages, so ask which one you are getting. Food is simple and government-canteen in style. The house has a long-running ghost story about Lady Morgan walking the corridors; that is local folklore, told cheerfully by staff and taxi drivers alike. Book on the WBTDC website, and check current status before you travel, since rates and room types change.
why: A 1930s heritage mansion at government-lodge prices
Durpin hill quiet, with the monastery a short walk away
Clear Kanchenjunga views from the lawn between October and April

faqs.q: How do I book Morgan House in Kalimpong?
faqs.a: Morgan House is run by West Bengal Tourism Development Corporation, so you book it through the WBTDC online booking site or their Kolkata and Siliguri offices. Rooms on weekends, in October and around the Durga Puja holidays sell out weeks ahead. Pay in full at booking, keep the voucher on your phone and carry an ID. Rates and room types change: check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Morgan House really haunted?
faqs.a: The ghost of Lady Morgan is a local story, not a recorded fact. Staff and drivers tell it with a smile, and it has made the house famous on Bengali travel shows. What you will actually notice is a quiet old stone house with long corridors and creaking floors. If ghost tales spoil your sleep, ask for a room in the newer cottage block.

faqs.q: How far is Morgan House from Kalimpong town?
faqs.a: It is about 3 km from the Motor Stand on Durpin hill, a 10–15 minute taxi ride for roughly ₹200–300. Walking down to town takes about 45 minutes and is pleasant in daylight, but the walk back up is steep. Zang Dhok Palri monastery and the golf course are within 15 minutes on foot, so many guests skip the town on their first evening.

name: Tashiding Tourist Lodge
summary: A smaller colonial-era bungalow run by West Bengal Tourism in the Morgan House grounds on Durpin hill. The same quiet setting and views as Morgan House, fewer rooms and usually a lower price.
body: Tashiding is the lesser-known sister of Morgan House: an old bungalow inside the same estate on Durpin hill, managed by West Bengal Tourism (WBTDC). Do not confuse it with Tashiding monastery in West Sikkim; this one is a guest house of a handful of rooms, with a sitting room, a garden and the same ridge-top quiet that makes Morgan House popular.

Because it is small, it suits families or two couples travelling together who want the Durpin setting without paying for the bigger house. Meals come from the Morgan House kitchen or are cooked to order; confirm when you book. As with every government lodge, upkeep varies year to year, so read recent traveller comments and check current status before you travel.
why: Same Durpin estate as Morgan House, usually cheaper
Small, so it is calm even on busy weekends
Walking distance to Zang Dhok Palri monastery

faqs.q: Is Tashiding Tourist Lodge the same as Morgan House?
faqs.a: No. Both are run by West Bengal Tourism and share the same estate on Durpin hill, but Tashiding is a separate, smaller colonial bungalow with its own rooms. Guests can walk the Morgan House lawns. If Morgan House is full on your dates, Tashiding is the natural second choice and is often a little cheaper.

faqs.q: Is this the Tashiding in Sikkim?
faqs.a: No. Tashiding monastery is in West Sikkim, near Yuksom and Pelling, about four hours away by road. Tashiding Tourist Lodge is a government guest house in Kalimpong town, on Durpin hill. Check the address on your booking voucher, because mix-ups do happen when people search online.

faqs.q: Does Tashiding Tourist Lodge serve food?
faqs.a: Meals are usually available from the lodge or the Morgan House kitchen next door: plain Indian and Chinese dishes, eggs and toast for breakfast. Tell the staff your dinner order by late afternoon. For momos and thukpa, take a taxi down to town, about ₹200–300 one way; check current status before you travel as kitchen arrangements change.

name: Holumba Haven
summary: A family-run guesthouse inside a working orchid nursery about 1 km below Kalimpong town. Cottages among the plant beds, home-style meals on order, and owners who know the local walks well.
body: Kalimpong has grown and sold orchids, gladioli and cacti for generations, and Holumba Haven lets you sleep inside that story. The guesthouse sits in the family's nursery, known as Nurseryman's Haven, about 1 km below the town on the Siliguri side. The land has been in the family for decades; it opened to guests in 2004, and its cottages are scattered across about two acres of gardens where some 250 orchid species grow.

The oldest building, Magnolia Cottage, has a literary footnote: the British Buddhist writer Sangharakshita wrote his memoir Facing Mount Kanchenjunga there. Meals are home-style and cooked on order, so tell the kitchen in advance. It is a calm base for two or three nights, close enough to walk into town for the haat bazaar and far enough to sleep well.
why: Sleep in a working orchid nursery
Owners who can plan village walks and day trips
Walkable to town, quieter than the Main Road hotels

faqs.q: Where exactly is Holumba Haven?
faqs.a: It is about 1 km below Kalimpong town on the road towards Siliguri, inside the family's orchid nursery. From the Motor Stand a taxi costs around ₹150–200, or you can walk in 15–20 minutes downhill. Ask the shared jeep from Siliguri to drop you at the gate on the way up, which saves the ride back down from town.

faqs.q: Can I see the orchids if I am not staying there?
faqs.a: The nursery is a working business, so ask politely at the gate rather than walking in. Orchids flower mainly from March to May, with some species in autumn. If you want a bigger tour of Kalimpong's plant trade, combine it with the cactus collection at Pine View Nursery near the town; check current status before you travel as opening hours vary.

faqs.q: Does Holumba Haven serve meals?
faqs.a: Yes, home-style meals are served in the dining room, but only on pre-order, so tell the kitchen what you would like in the morning for dinner and in the evening for breakfast. Expect dal, rice, seasonal vegetables, eggs and Tibetan or Nepali dishes. For street food, the town's momo shops are a 20-minute walk uphill.

name: Sailabash Eco Tourism Centre
summary: A West Bengal Forest Development Corporation (WBFDC) lodge in the Kalimpong forest compound. Simple rooms in a green, quiet corner of town, booked online through WBFDC, useful as a cheap base before heading on to Lava or Lolegaon.
body: The forest department has kept a compound in Kalimpong since the early forest-survey years, and the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation now runs part of it as the Sailabash Eco Tourism Centre. It is a practical, no-frills base: clean rooms in categories from deluxe to premium, trees around you, and the town within reach by a short taxi ride.

It pairs well with WBFDC's own lodges at Lava and Lolegaon, which are booked through the same website, so you can plan a three-lodge forest circuit in one sitting. Bookings usually open about three months ahead and get taken quickly for October, December and the spring holidays. Rates are indicative; check current status before you travel.
why: Government forest lodge prices inside town
Books on the same WBFDC site as Lava and Lolegaon
Green compound, quieter than the bazaar hotels

faqs.q: How do I book WBFDC lodges in Kalimpong district?
faqs.a: WBFDC lodges, including Sailabash in Kalimpong and the eco tourism centres at Lava and Lolegaon, are booked on the corporation's website, wbfdc.net. Bookings usually open about three months ahead. Pay online, carry the printed or phone voucher and a photo ID. Rates and room categories change: check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is food available at Sailabash?
faqs.a: Government forest lodges usually have a small kitchen that cooks simple meals to order: rice, dal, vegetables, eggs, sometimes chicken. Order dinner by late afternoon. Kalimpong town is close enough that most guests eat at least one meal at a momo shop or a Tibetan kitchen near the Motor Stand.

faqs.q: Is Sailabash a good base for Lava and Lolegaon?
faqs.a: It is a sensible first night. From Kalimpong, Lava is about 30–34 km and Lolegaon about 55 km, so you can drive on the next morning. Many travellers book Sailabash, Lava and Lolegaon together on the WBFDC website, spending one or two nights at each.

name: Deolo Tourist Lodge
summary: West Bengal Tourism's lodge on the top of Deolo hill, 1,704 m, the highest point around Kalimpong. Wake up above the town with Kanchenjunga to the north, gardens and the paragliding take-off at the door.
body: Deolo Tourist Lodge sits inside the Deolo tourist complex at the top of the hill, about 5–6 km above Kalimpong's Motor Stand. The hill is the town's highest point and its water tank: two reservoirs here store water for Kalimpong. By day the lawns fill with families, pony rides and paragliders taking off over the Relli valley; by evening the day visitors go home and the lodge guests have the hill to themselves.

The reason to stay is the dawn. On clear mornings between October and April, Kanchenjunga lights up to the north, and you can see the Teesta valley and the hills of Sikkim around you. Rooms are plain government-lodge rooms; ask for one facing north. Book on the WBTDC website and check current status before you travel.
why: The only place to sleep on top of Deolo
Sunrise over Kanchenjunga from your doorstep
Quiet evenings after the day visitors leave

faqs.q: Is it worth staying on Deolo hill rather than in Kalimpong town?
faqs.a: For one night, yes, if you want sunrise. The lodge is at 1,704 m, above the town's haze, and on clear mornings Kanchenjunga is in front of you without a drive in the dark. For longer stays, town or Durpin is more convenient for food and shopping. Many people do one night on Deolo and two in town.

faqs.q: Is there an entry fee to Deolo hill?
faqs.a: Day visitors pay a small entry fee to the Deolo park complex, usually under ₹100 per person, with extra for cameras or vehicles at times. Lodge guests normally do not pay again once checked in. Fees change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I paraglide from Deolo?
faqs.a: Yes. Tandem paragliding flights take off from Deolo hill most clear days outside the monsoon, run by private operators. Expect about ₹2,500–4,500 for a 10–25 minute flight, depending on length. Flights stop in rain, strong wind and cloud. Check the operator's licence and safety gear, and check current status before you travel.

name: Lava Eco Tourism Centre (WBFDC)
summary: The West Bengal Forest Development Corporation's cottages and tents in the Lava forest compound, at about 2,200 m. Misty, cold, quiet and good value, with the Neora Valley forest office and the monastery a short walk away.
body: The forest corporation made Lava known to Bengali travellers, and its eco tourism centre in the forest compound is still the most popular stay in the village. Standard and deluxe cottages sit on a slope among tall trees, with tents in season. The cottages with the best views need a climb up steep steps, which matters if you travel with older parents or small children; ask for a lower cottage if needed.

There is no restaurant around the compound, so meals come from the WBFDC canteen and must be ordered in advance. Bookings open about three months ahead on wbfdc.net and go fast for October and December. It is cold at night most of the year, so pack a fleece even in May. Check current status before you travel.
why: Sleep inside the forest at government prices
Short walk to the Neora Valley range office and the monastery
Cottages and tents for different budgets

faqs.q: How do I book the WBFDC cottages at Lava?
faqs.a: Book online at wbfdc.net, where the Lava Eco Tourism Centre is listed with its room categories. Bookings usually open about three months ahead and the October, Christmas and May dates go quickly. Carry the voucher and an ID. Rates and room types change: check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is food available at the Lava forest lodge?
faqs.a: Yes, through the WBFDC canteen, but you must pre-order. Tell the canteen your dinner by late afternoon and breakfast the night before. Meals are simple: rice, dal, vegetables, eggs and chicken. Lava bazaar, a 10-minute walk, has small momo and noodle shops for snacks.

faqs.q: Is the Lava forest lodge suitable for elderly travellers?
faqs.a: Partly. The cottages with the best views are reached by steep steps, which can be hard for older people or small children. Ask for a cottage close to the parking area when you book or on arrival. Nights are cold, around 2–8 °C in winter, so check that heaters or extra blankets are available.

name: Lolegaon Eco Tourism Centre (WBFDC)
summary: The forest corporation's lodge at Lolegaon, the Lepcha ridge village at 1,675 m. Plain cottages near the heritage forest and canopy walk, government rates, and the Jhandi Dara sunrise point a short drive away.
body: Lolegaon became a travel name in the 1990s, when the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation set up tents and cottages on the ridge. The eco tourism centre is still the anchor of the village's tourism, with rooms from deluxe to premium. It is a short walk from the heritage forest of old oak and cypress where the canopy walk runs, so you can be on the hanging bridge before the day trippers from Lava arrive.

Food comes from the lodge kitchen on order. The Jhandi Dara sunrise point is about 4–5 km away; arrange a car the night before or walk in the dark with a torch and a local guide. Bookings are on wbfdc.net, usually three months ahead. Check current status before you travel.
why: Walk to the canopy walk before the crowds
Government rates in a Lepcha ridge village
Same booking site as the Lava and Kalimpong forest lodges

faqs.q: How far is the WBFDC lodge from the Lolegaon canopy walk?
faqs.a: The heritage forest and canopy walk are a short walk from the forest lodge, around 10–15 minutes. Go at opening time in the morning for the quietest crossing. There is a small entry fee for the canopy walk, and it can close for repairs or bad weather, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I book the Lolegaon forest lodge with Lava in one trip?
faqs.a: Yes. Both are WBFDC eco tourism centres listed on wbfdc.net, and many people book one or two nights at Lava, then one or two at Lolegaon, 24 km away. The drive between them takes about an hour by reserved car, which costs roughly ₹1,800–2,500.

faqs.q: What is the weather like at Lolegaon?
faqs.a: At 1,675 m, Lolegaon is milder than Lava: around 5–15 °C in winter and 15–25 °C in summer. Mist is common in the afternoon, and the monsoon from June to September is heavy, with leeches in the forest. The clearest Kanchenjunga mornings come from October to March.
